decisions.rationale: BrowserQueryOptionsBase adds supportedDialogKinds?: string[]. This browser transport option does not apply: Local and cloud use the Node SDK query API, whose dialog options are already configured independently.

resumeSseStream(query): boolean is a new Browser SDK export. Neither the Local adapter nor the standalone cloud worker uses the Browser SDK or its SSE query transport; no resume integration is needed for this Node SDK update.

suspendSseStream(query): boolean is a new Browser SDK export. Local and cloud queries run through the Node SDK; browser SSE suspension is outside the integration and is not a substitute for Zeros turn cancellation.

core.d.ts re-exports BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES and LEGACY_TOOL_NAME_ALIASES from ./sdk.js. The vendor owns this additive barrel change; existing Node imports remain valid. The constants' host contract test is reserved for P2 of PR #717.

ArtifactOutput adds optional owned flags to five artifact/asset output variants. P1 keeps the existing bounded tool-content/resource-link handling and does not map this provider flag to Zeros workspace ownership or new artifact UI.

CronCreateOutput adds nextFireAt?: number. Adoption of the native next-fire timestamp and the lifecycle wake-up source is reserved for P5 of PR #717; P1 does not claim scheduling or idle-retention support for the new field.

CronListOutput.jobs entries add nextFireAt?: number. P5 of PR #717 will adopt the timestamp together with the lifecycle wake-up source; P1 leaves current cron/tool handling unchanged and makes no next-fire scheduling claim.

BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES is a new readonly tuple of 54 canonical built-in tool names. P2 of PR #717 will add the tool-name contract test against this export. P1 does not change existing tool routing or infer product support merely from a name appearing in the SDK.

LEGACY_TOOL_NAME_ALIASES is a new Readonly<Record<string, string>> export. P2 of PR #717 will cover canonical and legacy names in the tool-name contract test; P1 preserves existing aliases and persisted native identities.

McpSdkServerConfig adds tools?: McpServerToolPolicy[] for host-registered SDK servers. Policy interpretation remains in the Node SDK/CLI. P1 adds no per-tool policy override and preserves existing MCP configuration and approval behavior in both placements.

Query.reloadPlugins options add addPlugins?: SdkPluginConfig[]. Existing reloadPlugins() calls remain valid. P6 of PR #717 will adopt additive plugin loading with its native refusal/hold semantics; no plugin is added by P1.

SDKControlElicitationRequest adds property_order?: string[]. P3 of PR #717 will adopt explicit elicitation field ordering. P1 leaves the current Local form mapping and the cloud worker's cancellation response unchanged; ordering support is not claimed here.

SDKControlGetContextUsageResponse adds category id, per-server mcpInstructions token shares, customAgents pluginId/path, and skills pluginName/pluginId/path metadata. Stable category rows and MCP shares are reserved for P4 of PR #717 in both the Local adapter and cloud worker. P1 adds no mapping for the optional plugin/path metadata.

SDKControlGetUsageResponse extends both behavior summaries with max_effort, workflow, always_on_context and large_tool_results, plus optional recommendations and fix objects. This usage API is experimental and remains unused; P1 does not expose or depend on it in Local or cloud.

SDKControlInitializeRequest.sdkMcpServerConfigs entries add tools?: McpServerToolPolicy[]. The Node wrapper owns this control-handshake serialization. Zeros uses query() rather than authoring initialize frames and P1 supplies no new SDK-server permission policy.

SDKControlMcpCallRequest adds result_not_for_model?: boolean, a capability-gated app-only result mode. Zeros does not issue these direct MCP control calls or enable this mode; existing agent tool results and their transcript handling are unchanged.

SDKControlMcpStatusRequest adds liveReply?: boolean for upstream CCR/Remote Control live event streams. Zeros Local and cloud run the Node SDK with stdio, not that upstream cloud transport; existing mcpServerStatus() calls keep the wrapper's normal response behavior.

SDKControlReloadPluginsRequest adds wire field add_plugins?: SdkPluginConfig[], corresponding to Query.reloadPlugins({ addPlugins }). P6 of PR #717 will adopt the public option with native absolute-path, managed-policy and transport restrictions; P1 retains no-argument reloads.

SandboxSettingsSchema adds optional allowNestedUserNamespaces. The CLI defaults it to false and owns native settings validation. P1 never enables it or changes Local permissions or cloud VM isolation; no new sandbox override is supplied.

Settings adds attributionProject, attributionProjectPolicy.default, sshHostCommands and sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces. These remain native SDK/CLI settings; P1 adds no Zeros preference, telemetry mapping, SSH command surface or sandbox override, and retains each placement's existing settings sources.
